Continuous physical-interval invariance follows from endpoint reactant depletion and nonnegative rates, only while provider is defined.
Both Euler stages e and v are explicitly checked; convex Heun endpoint then remains admissible; positivity is not claimed without step rejection.

Manufactured event-time inversion is correct under stated first-event and log-domain restrictions.
Accepted-state boundary approach is partial-time, does not snap or claim exact event time; no equilibrium-root uniqueness assumption appears.
Finite caps and typed incomplete exits prevent unbounded exploratory work.
